column3: NKJV includes “who had been dead,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead.”
Close to the Greek; “a litra” is rendered “a pound,” and “nard” as “spikenard.”
NKJV has “Judas Iscariot, Simon's son,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Judas Iscariot.”
NKJV has “she has kept this,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “so that she may keep it.”
NKJV has “in turn Andrew and Philip told Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.”
NKJV has “answered,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “answers.”
Close to the Greek; “fruit” is rendered “grain.”
NKJV has “will lose it,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “loses it.”
NKJV has “My Father,” where the Greek has “the Father.”
